sections.title: Sec 8 - General Obligations of Data Fiduciary
Sec 9 - Children and Persons with Disability

controls.title: Give each Data Principal a notice at or before the point of requesting consent
Notice itemises the personal data processed and the specific purpose
Notice explains how to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board
Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by clear affirmative action, and limited to data necessary for the purpose
Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it
On withdrawal, processing stops and Data Processors are made to stop, unless law requires retention
Records exist to prove that notice was given and consent obtained
Data Processors engaged only under a valid written contract
Reasonable security safeguards implemented (encryption or masking, access control, logging and monitoring, backups)
Breach response process notifies the Board and affected Data Principals within the prescribed timelines
Personal data is erased when the purpose is served or consent is withdrawn, unless law requires retention
Business contact of the DPO or designated person is published
Grievance redressal mechanism is available and responses are tracked against the prescribed period
Verifiable consent of a parent or lawful guardian obtained before processing a child's data
No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children, subject to notified exemptions
Significant Data Fiduciary: India-based DPO, independent data auditor, and periodic DPIA and audit
Data Principals can obtain a summary of their data and the parties it is shared with
Data Principals can request correction, completion, updating and erasure
Data Principals can nominate another person to exercise rights on death or incapacity
Cross-border transfers comply with restrictions notified by the Central Government
